correctness.rationale: A three-dimensional stable AR(1)-driven linear recurrence has a unique stationary covariance. Solving its cross- and lag-moment identities gives an explicit stationary variance and an exact signed difference against zero momentum. All denominators are positive on the open stability domain. The comparison polynomial has nonnegative quadratic coefficient and a negative value at momentum one; its constant term crosses zero exactly at the claimed increasing threshold, proving exhaustive strict comparison intervals and uniqueness. The standalone checker independently solves exact-rational Lyapunov equations for 270 parameter triples and verifies the two reversal witnesses; the general proof is analytical, not an extrapolation from testing.

originality.rationale: The stationary white-noise formula is expressly excluded from novelty, as established in Liu et al. (arXiv:2012.03636). Kühn and Rosenow (arXiv:2306.05300) give a broad covariance response and a different negative finite-range correlation law, without the positive-AR1 sharp comparison classification. Gadat et al. (arXiv:1609.04228) and Dang et al. (arXiv:2401.06738) investigate other stochastic momentum regimes. Targeted mathematical-research record queries and primary-source comparisons found no claim with the same full implication; a general covariance identity could facilitate deriving the result, and equivalent older work remains a residual risk.
residual_risks: General colored-noise transfer/covariance identities may enable derivation of the comparison after algebraic optimization; a stronger specialized prior result in filtering, control or stochastic approximation could be missed.

value.rationale: For a natural persistent-noise model, stationary squared error is a practical criterion for deciding whether fixed positive momentum helps or harms. The result identifies a nontrivial correlation-dependent necessary and sufficient threshold and a unique complete momentum crossover; an exact countervailing example keeps curvature, stepsize and momentum fixed and changes only the noise correlation. These are structural design boundaries, not a table recomputation or an arbitrary parameter slice.
